title: IEEE 754 Special Values, Subnormals and the Extremes of the Format
quickIdea: The two extreme exponent fields are reserved: all zeros carries zero and the subnormals, all ones carries infinity and NaN, so the largest finite number stops one exponent short.
remember: E = 0 and F = 0: positive or negative zero. The sign bit is kept, so +0 and -0 are different patterns that compare equal.
E = 0 and F not 0: subnormal, value = (-1)^s x 0.F x 2^(-126). There is no hidden 1, which is what makes the step to zero gradual.
E = 255 and F = 0: positive or negative infinity.
E = 255 and F not 0: NaN, the only value that is not equal to itself.
Largest finite single: (2 - 2^(-23)) x 2^127, about 3.40 x 10^38, pattern 0x7F7FFFFF.
Smallest positive normal 2^(-126), about 1.18 x 10^(-38); smallest positive subnormal 2^(-149), about 1.40 x 10^(-45); machine epsilon 2^(-23), about 1.19 x 10^(-7).
The spacing between representable numbers grows with the exponent: it is 2^(-23) near 1 and 2^(-3) near 2^20.

example.prompt: Which of these single-precision words is the largest finite positive number: 0x7F7FFFFF or 0x7F800000?
example.work: 0x7F7FFFFF has exponent field 1111 1110 = 254 and a fraction of all ones, so it is (2 - 2^(-23)) x 2^127, about 3.4028 x 10^38 - the largest finite value. 0x7F800000 has exponent field 1111 1111 and a zero fraction, so it is positive infinity, which is not a finite number at all and is larger than every finite value but cannot be used as one.
example.answer: 0x7F7FFFFF is the largest finite value; 0x7F800000 is infinity.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 2024 Set 2 Q.14 shows four single-precision words and asks for the largest number. The option with an all-ones exponent and an all-ones mantissa is NaN, so the largest finite number is the one with exponent 1111 1110 and a full mantissa.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2024 Set 2 Q.14: With the IEEE 754 single-precision layout, choose the largest floating-point number: (A) sign 0, exponent 0111 1111, mantissa all ones; (B) sign 0, exponent 1111 1110, mantissa all ones; (C) sign 0, exponent 1111 1111, mantissa all ones; (D) sign 0, exponent 0111 1111, mantissa all zeros.
variations.why: B is (2 - 2^(-23)) x 2^127, the largest finite value. A is about 2, C is NaN because the exponent is all ones with a non-zero mantissa, and D is exactly 1. The largest exponent field that still denotes a number is 254, not 255.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: What is the value of the single-precision word 0x00000001, and what is the value of 0x00800000?
variations.answer: 2^(-149), the smallest positive subnormal; and 2^(-126), the smallest positive normal.
variations.why: 0x00000001 has an all-zero exponent and a single 1 in the last fraction bit, so it is 2^(-126) x 2^(-23) = 2^(-149). 0x00800000 has exponent field 1 and a zero fraction, so it is 1.0 x 2^(-126).

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: How far apart are neighbouring single-precision numbers near 1 and near 2^20?
variations.why: The gap is 2^(-23) times the power of two of the exponent, so it scales with magnitude. This is why a float cannot represent 1 + 2^(-24) but can represent 2^20 + 0.125.

trap.what: Choosing the all-ones exponent as the largest number, or treating subnormals as zero.
trap.why: An all-ones exponent is not an exponent: with a zero fraction it is infinity and with a non-zero fraction it is NaN. And an all-zero exponent with a non-zero fraction is a subnormal, a real number smaller than the smallest normal, not zero.
trap.counterexample: 0x7FFFFFFF is NaN, not the largest number; 0x7F7FFFFF is. And 0x00000001 is 2^(-149), not 0, although it is closer to zero than any normal number.

check.question: What are the four special cases of the exponent field in single precision?
check.answer: All zeros with a zero fraction is zero; all zeros with a non-zero fraction is subnormal; all ones with a zero fraction is infinity; all ones with a non-zero fraction is NaN.
check.explanation: Everything else, that is E from 1 to 254, is a normal number with an implied leading 1 and the bias of 127.
